title: Validator Reward Rounding to Zero
impact: Validators may receive zero rewards for their work, especially in projects with many slots or when using low-decimal tokens (e.g., USDC), breaking the incentive loop.
description: In `SapienCore._distributeValidatorRewards`, the reward calculation `(totalRewards * validatorBasisPoints * weight) / (10000 * totalQuantity * totalAccurateWeight)` can round to zero if the denominator is larger than the numerator. This is highly likely with `SqrtStakeConsensus` where weights are small, or in projects with large `totalQuantityAvailable` and tokens like USDC (6 decimals).

title: Liveness Griefing via Reveal Delay
impact: Malicious validators can delay the finalization of any contribution by up to 3 days (the default reveal deadline), stalling contributor rewards and project progress.
description: Consensus is only 'ready' in `ValidationOracle` when `minValidations` is met AND all pending commits have either revealed or expired. A validator can commit and then simply not reveal, forcing the protocol to wait for the full `revealDeadline` (default 3 days) before `getConsensus` returns a ready report.

title: Validator Queue Monopoly by Whales
impact: A single whale validator can claim all available validation slots for a project, preventing other validators from participating and potentially controlling the consensus outcome (subject to the 30% cap in some algorithms).
description: While contributors are limited by `MAX_CLAIMS_PER_USER`, validators in `ValidationOracle` are only limited by their `capacity` (locked stake). A whale can set a very high capacity and call `claimToValidate` repeatedly to fill the `pendingQueue` for all project contributions.

title: Reward Rate Manipulation (Sandwiching)
impact: Users can manipulate the reward-per-slot by frontrunning or backrunning `finalizeContribution` with `fundProject` calls, potentially extracting more value or diluting others' rewards.
description: The reward per contribution is calculated dynamically at the time of finalization using the current `totalRewardsAvailable` and `totalQuantityAvailable`. Since `fundProject` can increase these values at any time, the reward rate for a contribution submitted days ago can be changed right before it is finalized.

title: Strategic Non-Reveal to Evade Slashing
impact: Validators may choose to withhold reveals if they observe that their committed score will be an outlier, opting for the non-reveal slash instead of the outlier slash if it is lower.
description: Validators observe others' reveals before revealing their own. If the outlier slash (which can be up to 100% of stake) is higher than the non-reveal slash (100% of `committedStake`), they are incentivized to reveal. However, if they have external incentives or if the outlier detection is perceived as unfair, they can strategically withhold reveals to influence the `weightedAverage` or `stdDev`.

title: Reputation Incentive Decoupling
impact: Validators have less incentive to maintain high reputation if the project uses `LinearStakeConsensus` or `SqrtStakeConsensus`, as their reputation score is ignored in weight calculations.
description: The `LinearStakeConsensus` and `SqrtStakeConsensus` algorithms do not use the `reputation` field from `ValidationInput`. This decouples the protocol's primary quality incentive (reputation) from the economic weight in these algorithms, making them purely stake-based.

title: Unreclaimable Reward Dust
impact: Small amounts of various reward tokens will accumulate and remain trapped in the `Rewards` contract due to integer division rounding down.
description: Both contributor and validator reward distributions round down. The remaining 'dust' stays in `projectRewards` mapping in the `Rewards` contract. There is no mechanism for the project originator or protocol admin to reclaim this dust after a project is completed.
